issues: The acceptance test for M3 fails because generateCsv is defined without a store parameter but the test calls generateCsv(store). This causes TypeScript errors (expected 0 arguments, got 1) and runtime errors as the function uses getStore() which is not initialized in the test environment.

TypeScript compilation errors in src/lib/exportPdf.ts and src/screens/ExportScreen.tsx: they reference FileSystem.documentDirectory, but the expo-file-system typings do not expose a documentDirectory property, resulting in TS2339 errors.
The exportCsv and exportPdf modules should accept an optional Store argument to be testable, defaulting to the global store via getStore() when not provided.

ExportScreen calls generateCsv() and generatePdf() without passing a store, but after fixing the functions to accept an optional store, ExportScreen must be updated to call them without arguments (or pass getStore()).
Missing import of getStore in exportCsv (currently referencing getStore from './storage' which returns a singleton Store; ensure the correct import path is used).

The UI flow test for export expects a Snackbar with "Export ready to share" after clicking Export CSV. ExportScreen sets snack on success, but the exportCsv function may throw due to the store issue, causing the Snackbar not to appear. Fixing generateCsv will resolve this.
feedback: Adjust the CSV export helper to accept a Store parameter (or a generic data source) and update the test and app code accordingly. Also fix the PDF export helper to avoid using FileSystem.documentDirectory directly, either by using FileSystem.cacheDirectory (which is typed) or by casting to any. Ensure the TypeScript errors are resolved and the acceptance tests for M3 pass.
